items.title: Steve Buckingham, interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 25, 2019 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: And if you listen to that alto solo, it was by a guy named Jay Scott, who couldn’t read music, but he had an amazing sound.

ctx.x: I can hear it now that you said that, yeah.

And I told them I said I want this to sound like New York on a rainy night. And if you listen to that alto solo, it was by a guy named Jay Scott, who couldn’t read music, but he had an amazing sound. And he did that thing with the alto and the tenor at the same time and all that sort of thing. Not in the studio of course. But he could do it. But that alto solo in “Night Life” I just said, “wet streets of New York.” And that was I think the second take, that solo. That was an overdub. It wasn’t off the floor live.…

think I ever added a lute to anything but at some times I’d make a note for an English horn or a bassoon or something like that. That would be the orchestra dates. And then whatever the instrument I wanted to feature, sometimes a couple of French horns or something like that, we’d have to mic certain ways. There’s a real technique to micing a string section in an orchestra, brass and woodwinds, that type of thing. But I would make notes about — I’d put bassoon question mark you know, and then we’d come back. And…
